title: Present Continuous for Future Plans
tagline: arrangements: am / is / are + -ing + a future time
why: When something is already arranged, like an appointment, a booking or a meeting with friends, English speakers usually use the present continuous. It is the most natural way to talk about your calendar.
able: talk about your appointments and weekend plans
ask What are you doing on Saturday? and answer naturally
choose between present continuous, going to and will
mistakes: I see the doctor tomorrow at 10.
I'm seeing the doctor tomorrow at 10.
What do you do on Saturday evening?
What are you doing on Saturday evening?
We flying to Calgary next Tuesday.
We're flying to Calgary next Tuesday.
I will have lunch with a client at one. It's booked.
I'm having lunch with a client at one. It's booked.
A: Can you come tomorrow? B: Sorry, I work late.
A: Can you come tomorrow? B: Sorry, I'm working late.
use: Arrangements: plans with a time, a place or other people, often booked: I'm having lunch with Sara on Thursday.
Always with a future time, so the listener knows it is not now: We're flying to Montreal next Friday.
Timetables use the present simple: The bus leaves at 8:05. The film starts at 7.
Compare: I'm seeing the dentist at 3. (arranged) / I'm going to get fit. (intention) / I'll call you back. (decided now)
form: I'm meeting Tom at six. She's flying home on Sunday. They're coming tonight.
We aren't coming to the party on Saturday. I'm not working tomorrow.
What are you doing tonight? Are you working on Sunday?
signals: tonight, tomorrow, at 3 o'clock, on Friday, next week, this weekend; words like booked, appointment, tickets, in my calendar
tip: If it is in your calendar (a time, a place, other people), use the present continuous. If it is just an idea in your head, use going to. If you decide now, use will.

pick.q: I ___ the dentist at 3 o'clock tomorrow. It's in my calendar.
pick.why: An appointment with a time is an arrangement, so use the present continuous: I'm seeing the dentist.

pick.q: What ___ this weekend? Do you want to go for a hike?
pick.why: To ask about someone's plans, use the present continuous: What are you doing this weekend?

pick.q: We ___ to Montreal on Friday. The tickets are booked.
pick.why: A booked trip is an arrangement: we are flying. Don't forget are.

pick.q: Sorry, I can't come on Saturday. I ___ my sister move house.
pick.why: This is already arranged with your sister, so use the present continuous: I'm helping.
Timetables use the present simple, with -s for it: The film starts at 7:30.

pick.q: One day I ___ open my own restaurant. It's my dream.
pick.why: A dream with no fixed date is an intention, so use going to: I'm going to open a restaurant.

pick.q: A: Are you free on Thursday evening? B: No, I ___ dinner with my in-laws.
pick.why: B already has an arrangement, so use the present continuous: I'm having dinner with them.

pick.q: A: My car's at the garage. B: No problem. I ___ you to work tomorrow.
pick.why: B offers at that moment, so use will. Nothing was arranged before.

type.q: I ___ (meet) my accountant at 10 tomorrow. It's all booked.
type.why: A booked meeting is an arrangement: I'm meeting my accountant. (Going to is also OK.)

type.q: What ___ (you / do) on Saturday night? Any plans?
type.why: Asking about plans: What are you doing on Saturday night?

type.q: We ___ (not / come) to the party on Friday. We're away that weekend.
type.why: A negative arrangement: We aren't coming to the party.

type.q: My parents ___ (stay) with us next week. I've made up the spare bed.
type.why: This visit is arranged: My parents are staying with us next week.

type.q: ___ (you / work) on Monday? It's a holiday.
type.why: Asking about someone's arrangements: Are you working on Monday?

type.q: She ___ (have) a party for her 40th on Saturday. Everyone's invited.
type.why: The guests are invited, so it is arranged: She's having a party on Saturday.

type.q: I ___ (play) tennis with Mark at 6 tomorrow.
type.why: A time and another person make it an arrangement: I'm playing tennis with Mark.

type.q: They ___ (get) married in June. They've already booked the hall.
type.why: The hall is booked, so it is arranged: They're getting married in June.

spot.q: Tomorrow I go to the dentist at 3.
spot.why: A personal appointment uses the present continuous, not the present simple: I'm going to the dentist.

spot.q: What do you do tonight? Do you want to see a film?
spot.why: For plans, ask with the present continuous: What are you doing tonight?

spot.q: We will have dinner with my boss on Friday. She booked the table.
spot.why: The table is booked, so it is an arrangement: We're having dinner with my boss.

spot.q: I'm sorry, I can't come. I working late tonight.
spot.why: Don't forget am: I'm (I am) working late tonight.

spot.q: Are you come to the meeting tomorrow?
spot.why: Present continuous questions need -ing: Are you coming to the meeting?

order.a: I am meeting my friends at the mall tonight.
alt: I am meeting my friends tonight at the mall.
Tonight I am meeting my friends at the mall.
order.why: Subject + am + -ing + who + where + when: I am meeting my friends at the mall tonight.

order.a: What time are you leaving tomorrow morning?
order.why: Question word + are + you + -ing + time: What time are you leaving?

order.a: We are not going away this weekend.
alt: This weekend we are not going away.
order.why: Negative: are + not + -ing. We are not going away this weekend.

order.a: Is your brother coming to dinner on Sunday?
order.why: Question: Is + subject + -ing + the rest: Is your brother coming to dinner?

pick.q: I ___ my mother for lunch on Sunday. We booked a table for noon.
pick.why: The table is booked, so it is an arrangement: I'm meeting my mother.

pick.q: Are you ___ to the wedding next month?
pick.why: The present continuous needs -ing: Are you going to the wedding?

pick.q: Our flight ___ at 6:45 tomorrow morning, so we need to get up early.
pick.why: A timetable uses the present simple, with -s for it: Our flight leaves at 6:45.

pick.q: A: The fridge is empty. B: Okay, I ___ some food tonight.
pick.why: B decides at that moment, so use will: I'll order some food.

pick.q: He ___ his new job on Monday. He signed the contract yesterday.
pick.why: This is arranged (the contract is signed): He is starting his new job on Monday.

pick.q: We ___ working tomorrow. It's Canada Day.
pick.why: Negative present continuous: are + not + -ing. We aren't working tomorrow.

type.q: I ___ (see) the optometrist at 2:30 on Thursday.
type.why: An appointment with a time: I'm seeing the optometrist on Thursday.

type.q: Where ___ (you / go) on holiday this summer? Have you booked anything?
type.why: Asking about booked plans: Where are you going this summer?

type.q: My daughter ___ (not / come) home for Christmas this year.
type.why: A negative arrangement: My daughter isn't coming home.

type.q: We ___ (drive) to Quebec City on Saturday morning.
type.why: A trip with a day and time: We're driving to Quebec City on Saturday.

type.q: ___ (they / bring) the kids to the barbecue tomorrow?
type.why: Asking about arrangements: Are they bringing the kids?

type.q: I ___ (have) my hair cut at 4 tomorrow.
type.why: A booked appointment: I'm having my hair cut at 4.

type.q: He ___ (fly) to London next Tuesday. His company booked the ticket.
type.why: The ticket is booked, so it is arranged: He's flying to London.

type.q: Who ___ (you / take) to the party on Friday?
type.why: Asking about plans with other people: Who are you taking to the party?

spot.q: She is visit her grandparents next weekend.
spot.why: The present continuous needs be + -ing: She is visiting her grandparents.

spot.q: We meet the new neighbours for coffee tomorrow at ten.
spot.why: An arrangement with a time and other people: We're meeting the neighbours.

spot.q: Do you come to my party on Friday?
spot.why: To ask about someone's plans, use the present continuous: Are you coming to my party?

spot.q: I'm going to the dentist at nine tomorrow, so I'm late for work.
spot.why: The first part is right. The result is a future prediction, so use will: I'll be late for work.

order.a: We are having a barbecue on Saturday afternoon.
alt: On Saturday afternoon we are having a barbecue.
order.why: Subject + are + -ing + time: We are having a barbecue on Saturday afternoon.

order.a: Are you coming to the office tomorrow?
She is not working next Monday.
alt: Next Monday she is not working.
order.why: Negative: is + not + -ing + time. She is not working next Monday.

bank.q: I ___ my sister up at the airport at 5 tomorrow.
bank.why: A plan with a time and a place: I'm picking my sister up at 5.

bank.q: A: What ___ tonight? B: Nothing much. Just relaxing at home.
bank.why: Asking about plans for tonight: What are you doing tonight?

bank.q: The last bus ___ at midnight, so don't be late.
bank.why: A bus timetable uses the present simple: The last bus leaves at midnight.

bank.q: My cousins ___ to visit us next week. They booked their flights yesterday.
bank.why: The flights are booked, so it is arranged: My cousins are coming.

bank.q: A: I'm thirsty. B: Sit down. I ___ you a glass of water.
bank.why: B offers at that moment, so use will: I'll get you some water.

bank.q: One day we ___ travel around the world.
bank.why: A dream with no date is an intention, so use going to + base verb.

bank.q: I ___ working this Saturday, so I can come to your party.
bank.why: Negative present continuous: am + not + -ing. I'm not working this Saturday.

bank.q: ___ Raj and Priya coming to the wedding?
bank.why: Present continuous questions start with be: Are Raj and Priya coming?

bank.q: We ___ (have) friends over for dinner on Friday.
bank.why: Guests on a set day is an arrangement: We're having friends over.

bank.q: ___ (you / go) to the hockey game on Saturday? I have a spare ticket.
bank.why: Asking about someone's plans: Are you going to the game?

bank.q: I ___ (not / work) tomorrow. I took the day off.
bank.why: The day off is arranged: I'm not working tomorrow.

bank.q: She ___ (move) to Winnipeg next month. The truck is booked.
bank.why: The truck is booked, so it is arranged: She's moving next month.

bank.q: I ___ (take) my car to the garage at eight tomorrow.
bank.why: An appointment with a time: I'm taking my car to the garage.

bank.q: My husband and I go to a concert on Saturday night.
bank.fix: My husband and I are going
opts: My husband and I are going
bank.why: A one-time event that is arranged uses the present continuous: we are going to a concert.

bank.q: I'm meeting the landlord at four to sign the lease.
bank.why: This sentence is correct. A meeting with a time is an arrangement, so the present continuous is right.

bank.q: She is fly to Halifax on Monday.
bank.why: The present continuous needs be + -ing: She is flying to Halifax.

bank.q: The train leaves at 7:10 tomorrow morning.
bank.why: This sentence is correct. Timetables use the present simple, even for the future.

bank.a: I am having dinner with my parents tonight.
alt: Tonight I am having dinner with my parents.
bank.why: Subject + am + -ing + who + when: I am having dinner with my parents tonight.

bank.a: When are you flying back to Toronto?
bank.why: Question word + are + you + -ing: When are you flying back?

bank.a: We are not going to the cottage this weekend.
alt: This weekend we are not going to the cottage.
bank.why: Negative: are + not + -ing + place + time.
